title: Tighten a 6 mm bit in a keyed drill chuck: keep the key's pinion meshed as the torque rises, then take the key out
instruction: Fit the 6 mm drill bit in the drill's chuck, centered and tightened with the chuck key, then take the key out.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (1.53 million in the US, BLS May 2025) "repair machines, equipment, or structures, using tools such as hammers, hoists, saws, drills, wrenches" (O*NET 49-9071.00). A keyed chuck holds nothing until it is tightened, and only its key tightens it: Bosch's steps are "Insert the tool. Insert the chuck key into the corresponding holes of the key type drill chuck and clamp the tool uniformly", and its warning "Remove any adjusting key or wrench before turning the power tool on. A wrench or a key left attached to a rotating part of the power tool may result in personal injury" (GBM 10 RE manual). The skill is the key: its 6 mm pilot in the hole and its pinion in the sleeve's teeth while the torque rises and the teeth push it out, the other hand holding the drill, until three jaws close centred on the shank and pass a holding test; then the key comes out. No bit is chosen and nothing is driven.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. A Bosch GBM 10 RE corded drill, keyed-chuck version (3 601 D73 5..; 225 long, 200 high, 1.3 kg; blue plastic housing 62 x 155 x 70, black handle), unplugged, lies on its side on the bench: chuck axis along y, 35 above the bench, chuck nose at x 240, y -100 pointing to the robot's right, handle pointing toward the robot (its foot at x 71 to 91, y 30 to 75). Chuck: Bosch 10 mm keyed chuck (1 to 10 mm, 3/8"-24), steel, knurled sleeve 32 across and 30 long from the nose, body 33 across to 56 behind the nose, then the 43 mm spindle collar; its three round jaws (4 across) are opened to 7.5 mm; a fully pushed-in shank stops 34 in. One of its key holes (6.4 mm, 7 deep, 37 behind the nose) faces straight up. The bit: a 6 mm HSS twist drill (DIN 338, 93 long, 36 of plain shank, 14 g) lies across two wooden blocks (40 x 20, 32 high, centred at x 240, y -290 and y -225) on the chuck's axis line, shank end at y -207 toward the chuck. The key: the chuck's own steel T-handle chuck key (Bosch replacement key type D: 6 mm pilot, 10-tooth pinion 12 across, 40 from pilot tip to the 110 x 8 x 8 bar; 50 g) hangs by its bar in a wooden key rest (120 x 80, 48 high, with a 50 x 60 slot through it) centred at x 120, y -170, bar along x. README.md lists every collider.
scoring: Judged after the run with a ruler, a fixed pointer, a spring scale and a 100 mm bar clamped to the flutes. Key out: the key's pilot at least 30 mm from the key hole (not in any hole). Captured: at least 20 mm of the shank between the jaws (at most 73 mm of bit stands out of the nose). Centred: turned one turn by hand, the bit's axis 50 mm in front of the nose stays within 1 mm of the chuck's axis. Gripped: all three jaws on the shank. Secure: the bit does not turn in the jaws under 0.5 N m (5 N at the bar's end) for 2 s, nor slip under a 20 N pull; in the simulation, the chuck was tightened to at least 0.30 N m at the key. 1.0 (success): key out, bit captured, centred, gripped and secure, both grippers at least 3 cm clear of the drill, the bit and the key, drill and bit still (under 1 mm in 0.5 s), held 1 s. 0.5: key out, bit captured, centred and gripped, short of that (not secure, a hand not clear, or not yet still for 1 s). 0.25: key out, bit at least 5 mm in the chuck (its shank end between the jaws, within 5 mm of the chuck's axis; the bit within 15 degrees of the axis) and either not gripped (lying in the open jaws) or gripped centred with under 20 mm in. 0: the key left in the chuck, no bit in the chuck, the bit clamped off-centre (more than 1 mm out 50 mm in front: crooked), or, at the end, the drill fallen off the bench or out past its edge (its centre of mass below the bench top or outside the 1,100 x 1,300 mm top: x -190 to 910, y -650 to 650). Lifting, tipping or moving the drill over the bench is allowed and costs nothing by itself.
reset_notes: Loosen the chuck with the key to a 7.5 mm opening (a 7.5 mm gauge pin just slides between the jaws), lay the bit back across its two blocks, hang the key in its rest, turn the chuck so a key hole faces straight up, and lay the drill back on its side where it was. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz. PhysX cannot mesh the key's pinion or drive the jaws, so the chuck is modelled: the sleeve turns only with the pilot seated in the hole, 0.5 mm per turn, +0.6 N m/rad past jaw contact, the teeth pushing the key out 18 N per N m. The bit is let go in the open jaws (7.5 mm; it rests on two); the modelled jaws lift it onto the axis, straight only if 20 mm in, and hold its depth unless a hand is at it. Estimated: those rates; jaw, hole, key sizes. Spindle fixed; no cord.
